newsitem.title: UK: EU needs radical sugar policy reform.
newsitem.headline: EU needs radical sugar policy reform.

text.p: The European Union (EU) needs a radical reform of its sugar policy to facilitate free internal movement of the commodity and encourage more competition among processors, an industry lobby group said on Friday.

Speaking at a two-day conference hosted by Agra Europe, Tom Harrison said the EU's current sugar regime was incompatible with the trading bloc's planned eastwards expansion and the trend in world trade patterns, and also with reforms in other regimes of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP).
Harrison, a former director of Mars Confectionery, said he was advancing the lobbying position of the association of the European Industrial users of Sugar (CIUS).

CIUS represents the sugar and isoglucose buying interests of the European food and beverage industries. Its members purchase and use almost 70 percent of the EU's annual consumption of these sweeteners through their incorporation in a wide variety of added-value products.

Harrison said the group's objective in the medium term was to arrive at a position where production was controlled solely through a single internal price, where this price was moved downwards to the point where production equated with consumption.
This could be achieved by eliminating the minimum beet price to break the direct link between price and processing margins and also by removing regional sugar premiums, he said.
The EU's sugar intervention price would have to be progressively reduced and national aids for sugar industries would also have to be phased out.
